blocks.text: The rain continued falling as I stood on that Boston sidewalk, staring at the woman I had mourned for three years.
My daughter, Lily, refused to let go of her.
The woman pressed her face against Lily’s hair.
“I missed you too, my little angel. Every single day.”
My name is Everett Langford. I was forty-two years old, the CEO of Langford Holdings, a multibillion-dollar investment corporation headquartered in Boston.
Except the one thing I had spent three years believing was impossible.
“Adriana?” I finally managed to whisper.
Her cheeks were thinner. Her hair was shorter, uneven, and tangled. Her clothes were soaked, and her hands trembled from the cold.
The same eyes I had fallen in love with twelve years earlier.
“Your funeral. Your death certificate. The hospital called me. Your mother identified your body!”
At the mention of my mother, Adriana’s expression changed.
“That’s exactly what she wanted you to believe.”
I immediately called my driver and ordered him to bring the car.
Then I wrapped my coat around Adriana and took her to a private medical clinic.
Lily sat beside her, holding her hand the entire journey.
I sat opposite them, unable to stop staring.
But the woman I remembered had disappeared somewhere during those three missing years.
After the doctors examined Adriana, they confirmed she was severely malnourished and suffering from several untreated medical conditions.
When Lily finally fell asleep in a nearby chair, Adriana asked me to close the door.
“Everett, before I tell you everything, you need to understand something. Your mother didn’t just hide me from you. She stole three years of my life.”
Three years earlier, Adriana had supposedly been involved in a terrible car accident outside Boston.
The police informed us that her vehicle had gone off a bridge during a storm.
The car was recovered several hours later.
A badly burned female body was supposedly discovered nearby.
The authorities identified the remains through personal belongings and dental records.
My mother, Margaret Langford, had handled most of the arrangements because I was overseas negotiating a major acquisition.
I returned just in time for the funeral.
She explained that on the night of the accident, she had received a phone call from Margaret.
My mother claimed Lily had been taken to the hospital after a serious medical emergency.
A black SUV blocked her vehicle on a quiet road.
Two men dragged her out, covered her face, and forced her into another car.
When she regained consciousness, she was in an unfamiliar room.
Her phone, identification, and belongings were gone.
Adriana said my mother delivered one sentence that changed everything.
“You are going to disappear, and my son will never know you existed.”
“Because I discovered what your mother had been doing with your company.”
Three months before the accident, Adriana had discovered suspicious financial transactions involving several companies owned by Langford Holdings.
Millions of dollars were being transferred into offshore accounts.
At first, she assumed it was ordinary corporate restructuring.
But the deeper she investigated, the worse things became.
She discovered that my mother had secretly established shell companies using forged authorization documents bearing my signature.
Over several years, nearly $80 million had disappeared.
She told her she would bring the evidence to me.
According to Adriana, my mother claimed that if the truth became public, I would lose the company, my reputation, and possibly my freedom.
“They kept me in a house outside the city,” Adriana continued. “I was watched constantly. They told me you believed I was dead. They showed me newspaper articles about your funeral.”
The second time, Margaret personally visited her.
“If you ever try to contact Everett again,” Margaret allegedly warned, “your daughter will grow up without either parent.”
“I was terrified, Everett. I thought staying away was the only way to keep Lily safe.”
For three years, I had believed I was the victim of a tragedy.
Now I understood that someone had deliberately destroyed my family.
The following morning, I went straight to my mother’s mansion in Beacon Hill.
Margaret was sitting in her sunroom, drinking tea.
“Everett! What a surprise. Is everything all right?”
I placed a photograph of Adriana on the table.
For the first time in my life, I saw genuine fear in my mother’s eyes.
“You don’t understand what you’re dealing with.”
“I did what I had to do to protect this family.”
“She was protecting my company from you!”
